items.headline: Modern Filesystem Benchmarks: Btrfs/ZFS/Bcachefs Under Real-World Workloads Released
bullets: Bartosz Fenski published comprehensive benchmarks testing bcachefs, btrfs, and ZFS on workloads classic benchmarks skip—snapshots, aging, compression, redundancy layouts, encryption, and fsync tail latency under degraded operation.
First real hardware results published after obtaining machines from Hetzner; GitHub Actions runners used for 590+ benchmark runs with calibration to filter unreliable VMs.

Benchmarks reveal substantial performance gaps between filesystems on actual multi-device deployments, particularly for CoW operations and snapshot aging—directly addressing gaps in standard Phoronix single-device synthetic tests that miss actual production deployment patterns.
items.novelty: First published real-hardware benchmark results on actual production-class CoW filesystem workloads that classic benchmarks deliberately exclude, including degraded-mode operation and snapshot aging curves.
